0.original: Your plan is set, but G'raha Tia is not without reservations.

48.original: To use this train as an explosive is a brazen plan. We'll have but one attempt, so we had best make it count!

50.original: Well, we have our plan. Now let's finish this train and blast our way into the dome.

51.original: We'll make this plan work─see if we don't!

52.original: While I have no objections to the plan itself, I have one concern.

53.original: How can we be certain Zoraal Ja will not strike Tuliyollal in retaliation?

55.original: But when my brother told me to come and prove myself, he meant it.

56.original: He wants to show that his kingdom is superior to Tuliyollal, and it'll give him no satisfaction to attack when he knows I'm not there.

57.original: No, he'll be waiting inside the dome. Waiting for us to challenge him so he can crush us and prove his strength.

58.original: Indeed... If anything, we're more likely to put Tuliyollal in danger by not taking the fight to him.

59.original: So we indulge Zoraal Ja. At least, until Tuliyollal has shored up its defenses.

60.original: Right. We'll charge in from the front and keep his eyes on us.

61.original: During which time Koana will find a way to fortify Tuliyollal.

62.original: If you believe this is the best course, then we shall trust in your judgment.

63.original: I expect there will be no small amount of enemy resistance, but we will do all in our power to assist you.

65.original: Well, time is of the essence. Let's go and see what's left to be done for the train.

66.original: Everyone's hard at work on the train. I can't wait to see how it turns out.

68.original: Shenza has given me a list of materials. We'll see to it they have everything they need!

69.original: It's a shame Cid and his engineers aren't here to help. If they were here, I expect they'd turn it into a flying train.

70.original: Zoraal Ja's forces remain quiet for now. If there is any movement, I'll alert everyone immediately.

71.original: Looks like work is getting underway. We'll finish in no time at all!

72.original: So what can we do to help? No need to hold back!

73.original: As I understand it, the two of you met your fair share of craftsmen during the rite of succession.

74.original: Would you happen to know a few who'd be willing to come and help us complete modifications to the train?

75.original: Of course! What sort of craftsmen did you have in mind?

77.original: Perhaps my greatest concern is keeping the train safe from enemy attacks.

78.original: Even with you all aboard to fend them off, it'd be over in an instant if they managed to get just one good hit on the ceruleum tanks.

79.original: According to eyewitnesses, the soldiers use lightning-based weapons, so I've a mind to install grounding rods. Would you happen to know a carpenter who could handle that?

82.original: We could ask the fellow with a fetish for formalities.

83.original: A master carpenter from Ok'hanu, eh? If they'd be willing, we'd be glad to have them.

84.original: No objections from me. Just be sure not to forget their traditional greeting...

85.original: Heh, you mean Wuk Evu. While he has his quirks, there's no questioning his carpentry!

86.original: A master carpenter from Ok'hanu, eh? If they'd be willing, we'd be glad to have them.

87.original: But we'll need more than just a carpenter if we want this done in a timely fashion.

88.original: We've got a lot of equipment that needs moving. <hex:021A020203>Heavy<hex:021A020103> equipment. I don't suppose you know anyone up to the task?

93.original: But I wouldn't exactly call him strong. For a task like this, I think we should ask someone like, say, Zurmurwur.

94.original: You're friends with the Yok Huy? I'll be damned. We'll not want for strength with help like that.

95.original: Zurmurwur would be perfect! We'd be hard-pressed to find folks stronger than the Yok Huy, and I'm sure he'd be willing to help.

96.original: You're friends with the Yok Huy? I'll be damned. We'll not want for strength with help like that.

97.original: Next, I'd like to outfit the train with some powerful weaponry of its own.

98.original: Like as not, the soldiers will be riding their flying vessels. We'll need countermeasures to deal with them.

99.original: That's true... I for one can't use magic, nor am I handy with a firearm like my brother.

100.original: Any ideas for ranged weapons we can use?

102.original: Let's borrow guns from Koana for everyone!

103.original: Let's install ballistas on the train! Big ones!

104.original: Guns, eh? While they'd be suitable in theory, it takes no ordinary marksman to hit a flying target.

105.original: So it'd need to be something that doesn't require that level of skill and precision. But weapons aren't exactly my field of expertise...

106.original: Ballistas, eh? While they'd be powerful, it seems to me it'd take too long to reload between shots.

107.original: If there were some sort of ballista that could reload quickly, then that might work. But weapons aren't exactly my field of expertise...

108.original: Perhaps I can be of assistance.

109.original: The Crystarium employed aetheric cannons for its defenses, and I see no reason why the design cannot be adopted for your train.

110.original: While I did not conceive them myself, I know their design. It should be possible to build them here, provided we have the requisite materials and skilled smiths.

111.original: Now, that sounds like something Fonjeantaine can help with. What are the materials we need?

112.original: The barrel can be fashioned from any metal, so long as it's highly conductive to aether. To power the cannon, we will require fire-aspected crystals of the highest purity.

113.original: Fire crystals, eh? Might be as the miners over at the Springs can help with that.

114.original: Then if I could leave the crystals and smiths in everyone's hands, I shall get started drawing up the schematics.

115.original: Right then, I'll secure us the smiths.

116.original: In the meantime, could you deal with the materials? Shenza is in charge of our supplies, so it might be good to talk to him about it first.

117.original: Well, I think we're set for a plan! Thanks for the consultation!

118.original: Now let's get this train dressed up, and give her the proper farewell she deserves!

119.original: Right. Time to put my knowledge gained in the First to use.

121.original: To make good speed, I'm going to try and enlist some more help from among our friends back in Yok Tural.

122.original: I'll leave the materials in your care. I think I saw Shenza over to the southeast.

123.original: That should be enough lumber for the armor. What else do we need...?

124.original: Oh! Sorry, I didn't see you there. What can I do for you?

125.original: Aetheric cannons? Interesting. I have an idea where we can get the conductive metal, so I'll take care of it.

126.original: I'm not sure about the fire crystals, though. Might be best if you spoke directly with a miner. Can I leave that to you?

128.original: You're friends with Iyaate, aren't you? One of the best miners around. If anyone can get you the crystals you're after, it's her.

129.original: Iyaate is sure to get you all the fire crystals you'd ever want, and then some.

130.original: Oh, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>. What brings you around these parts?

131.original: The purest fire crystals, you say?

132.original: I think I heard tell about them before, but what was that about...?
